log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Incineroar leads for Intimidate and Fake Out, which blunt the opponent's physical attackers like Garchomp and Kingambit. Garchomp is the fastest real attacker on the team, and Gholdengo adds strong special pressure that covers Sinistcha and Archaludon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since both teams mirror each other, I'm thinking Incineroar, Garchomp, and Kingambit give us the best matchup control with intimidate support and strong offense against their identical lineup.

decisions.thought: Both sides lead with Incineroar, and Fake Out is legal on this first turn. It has +3 priority, so it hits before the opponent's Incineroar moves and flinches it, giving me a free turn. Protect would only stall.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Both sides have Incineroar, so Fake Out is the standard turn-one play since it's unresisted and flinches the opponent, giving a free tempo advantage.

decisions.thought: Flare Blitz is weak here because Sinistcha's Heatproof halves Fire damage, and my Incineroar is already at -1 Attack. Parting Shot lowers Sinistcha's Attack and Sp. Atk, which blunts its main special offense, and gets Incineroar out for a fresh attacker such as Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the type matchup: Fire isn't resisted by Ghost, but Sinistcha's Heatproof ability halves the damage from Flare Blitz, and Fake Out was blocked since Ghost is immune to normal-type moves.

Flare Blitz looks weak given Heatproof and the attack drop, while Parting Shot could pivot into something like Gholdengo, whose Shadow Ball would hit Sinistcha's Ghost typing super effectively, though Thunderbolt would be resisted by Grass. Parting Shot's attack and special attack drops matter most since Sinistcha's special attack is its primary offensive stat.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is faster, so it will hit first, but Incineroar should survive and Flare Blitz is 2x super effective into Steel/Ghost. Parting Shot is useless since Good as Gold blocks status moves. Flare Blitz is the strongest play for a likely heavy hit or knockout.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at the matchup, Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing takes 2x from Incineroar's Fire moves like Flare Blitz, but Good as Gold makes it immune to status moves like Parting Shot. Gholdengo also outspeeds Incineroar, and its Ghost-type attacks like Shadow Ball hit neutrally against Incineroar's Dark typing while being super effective in other matchups.

Calculating damage, Flare Blitz from Incineroar should deal heavy damage to Gholdengo due to the Fire/Steel 2x weakness, likely dealing around 50%+ even accounting for recoil, making it the strongest offensive option despite Gholdengo probably attacking first.

decisions.thought: Our Incineroar is at -2 Attack, so Flare Blitz does little to the opposing Incineroar, which resists Fire. Garchomp takes the Fire hit neutrally and threatens a 2x Earthquake on Incineroar, with much higher speed and HP.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Our Incineroar is down at 143/202 with Attack lowered twice, while the opposing Incineroar is at full health. Flare Blitz would only be half-effective here since Fire is resisted by Fire/Dark typing, so I'm weighing whether that's still the right move given our lowered attack stat.

decisions.thought: Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar (169 vs 72-123), and Earthquake is super effective with STAB. Mega Garchomp raises Attack enough to make the knockout reliable even if the opposing Incineroar has a Sitrus Berry or a high-HP roll. I'll use Mega Earthquake now.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp's Earthquake hits Incineroar for solid super-effective Ground damage, so I'm estimating the damage roll using Garchomp's 182 Attack against Incineroar's roughly 99-156 Defense range to see if it threatens a KO.

Even without mega evolution, Earthquake likely KOs or nearly KOs the target, and saving the mega for later could be valuable since Garchomp is already fast and threatening. Stone Edge is an alternative, but Earthquake hits reliably in singles with no ally risk, so I'll go with it unmega'd for now.

decisions.thought: Sinistcha is Grass/Ghost, so Earthquake is resisted, but Outrage is neutral with 120 power and 100% accuracy. Garchomp outspeeds it, so this is a strong attacking turn. Outrage's confusion drawback is acceptable here, since Stone Edge has only 80% accuracy.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Garchomp's move options against Sinistcha's Grass/Ghost typing—Mega Earthquake is resisted, Outrage is neutral, and I'm working out whether Stone Edge gets a Rock-type advantage against Grass.

Weighing Outrage's higher accuracy and STAB power against Stone Edge's crit chance, and considering whether Swords Dance setup is safer given Garchomp's speed advantage and the remaining weak opposing threats.

decisions.thought: Only one legal action is available, so Outrage is the move. Garchomp-Mega outspeeds Sinistcha, and Outrage is a super-effective hit against a Grass/Ghost target.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: The only legitimate response here seems to be expressing outrage, so I need to think about how to format that.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp outspeeds Sinistcha, and Outrage is a reliable 100% accuracy STAB hit. Earthquake is resisted by Grass, and Stone Edge's 80% accuracy is a risk. Outrage's confusion comes later, so it's the best attack now.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Sinistcha's typing against Garchomp's moves—Earthquake is weakened by its Grass typing, and Outrage's Dragon type doesn't hit it super effectively since Grass resists Dragon somewhat, so I'm weighing whether Protect or Life Dew is the better play given the speed disadvantage.

Weighing the setup option against just continuing the attack, Outrage's reliable accuracy and STAB power make it the better choice over the riskier Stone Edge, so I'll go with Outrage.

decisions.thought: Outrage is the only legal action, and it's forced anyway since Garchomp is locked into it. Garchomp is faster than Sinistcha (158 vs 81-134), so it moves first and should knock out the 26% Sinistcha.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Garchomp is locked into Outrage from the previous turn, so Outrage is the only legal move here despite Sinistcha being low on HP. I'll just go with it.

decisions.thought: Sinistcha is at 33% and just used Protect, so it likely can't protect again this turn. Garchomp is faster, and Dragon and Ground are resisted by Grass/Ghost, while Rock is neutral. Stone Edge at 100 power with high crit ratio should KO the Sinistcha before it acts.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since Sinistcha protected last turn, it probably won't protect this turn, so Outrage or Stone Edge should connect — though Dragon is resisted by Grass while Rock is neutral against both Grass and Ghost, making Stone Edge the more reliable choice.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp is faster (158 vs 81-134), so it moves first. Sinistcha is at about 56% HP, roughly 90-100 HP. Outrage is 100% accurate, neutral on Grass/Ghost, and should knock it out. Stone Edge is less reliable at 80% accuracy.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking matchups: Garchomp Mega is low HP while Sinistcha, Grass/Ghost, sits near half health. I'm weighing how Outrage and Earthquake interact with Sinistcha's typing, noting Ground is only half-effective against Grass.

Running the damage math, Outrage with STAB should comfortably knock out Sinistcha at its current HP even against its higher defense rolls, and it's fully accurate while Stone Edge risks a miss. Since Garchomp outspeeds, Outrage is the clear choice this turn.

decisions.thought: Garchomp Mega is faster than Sinistcha and Outrage should KO the 10% Sinistcha before it can act. Only one legal action is available anyway.
